I've been working this land for 55 years. I know what grows here in Quzhou, I know my soil, and I know my limits. I'm 76 now — just the two of us at home — so I can't push myself the way I used to. But I'm not going to change what works.

**Wheat-maize rotation (14 mu):** This is the backbone. Every autumn I plant wheat on those 14 mu after rotary tillage, then after wheat harvest in June I go straight into summer maize with no-tillage — saves my back and keeps moisture in. I've used the same improved wheat variety for years, Jimai or similar. For maize I always buy hybrid seed from the county market, been doing that for 30 years, no reason to stop. I do a base fertilizer application before wheat, then topdress at jointing. For maize I split nitrogen — some at planting, rest at jointing. I water wheat three times: at planting, overwintering, and jointing. Maize I water twice unless it's a dry summer, then maybe three times. Pest pressure on wheat is mostly aphids and rust, so I spray twice. Maize I really only need one herbicide pass.

**Chili (4 mu):** I grow chili on a separate 4 mu plot. It's a good cash crop here. I use improved local varieties I trust. Chili drinks a lot of water — I'll irrigate five times through the season from the well. Aphids and blight are my main worries so I spray three times. I rotary till before transplanting.

**Cotton (3.4 mu):** Cotton is work, especially at picking time. But I've grown it all my life and I know the margins. I'll deep plough before planting in spring, use hybrid seed. I'm careful with cotton pests — bollworm, aphids — four sprays minimum. Three irrigations through the long season.

I won't experiment this year. At my age, I manage the risk.
